text:
maria: FYI canary p95 decode jumped ~1.9x after the merge that touched attention packing heuristics. Noticed mostly on shortseq workloads (<= 32)

jake: ugh. which merge/PR? any CI alerts? :eyes:

maria: PR #4821 — changed packing decisions so we favor tiled attention kernel for batched shortseq packing. CI perf job flagged a regression this morning (job perf/serve/p95).

ci-bot: Perf test perf/serve/p95 failed: baseline=62ms current=118ms (+90%). Regression window: builds 5077600000..5077769999.

sam: do we have a flamegraph or perf output? could be kernel selection flip + wrong launch config.

maria: attached a short snippet from perf-top and stack collapse I ran locally:

```
# perf top (summarized)
  32.1%  attention_kernel_tiled
  12.8%  attention_kernel_generic
  10.2%  gpu_dispatch
   8.9%  copy_kv_cache
   7.3%  decode_loop
```

# folded stacks showed attention_kernel_tiled dominating at shortseq, baseline runs used attention_kernel_generic

jake: did the kernel selector rule change thresholds? seems like tiled is more expensive for packed shortseq due to extra memory moves.

tanvi: I instrumented selector: commit 9f3cbd6 changed `prefer_tiled_for_batch=true` when avg_seq < 48 and batch_size>8. That sounds like it would flip our shortseq tests.

maria: exact. baseline (before merge) selected generic kernel for batch_size 16 seq 24; after merge it picks tiled. microbench (local) shows tiled path + KV prefetch memmove increases p95.

sam: plan: bisect from commit 9f3cbd6 -> HEAD of that PR. If confirmed, we either revert the selector tweak or tune threshold. Who can bisect?

jake: I can run quick git bisect on the PR branch. Locally I'll run the perf test harness (shortseq job). Bisect steps:
```
git checkout pr/4821
git bisect start -- bad HEAD -- good 9f3cbd6^
# run ./tools/bench_shortseq.sh (same harness as CI)
# mark good/bad until we find offending commit
```

maria: CI has a faster route: create minimal reproducer (batch 16 seq 24) and run against the canary image that CI used. I pushed a repro script to /tmp/repro_shortseq_{ts}.sh on the canary instance.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout suspended due to perf regression on tag: canary-2026-03-18-1 :no_entry_sign:

tanvi: I'll start the bisect now and report the exact commit if I can reproduce locally. If it's the selector tweak, I propose we change rule to prefer_tiled_for_batch only when avg_seq < 24 and batch_size >= 32 (safer).

sam: also add a quick guard in kernel selector: if memmove_estimate > threshold, force generic. That should avoid pathological KV copy cases.

jake: noted. Running bisect now, will post first 3 checkpoints.

maria: for tracing, add env var `REDWOOD_RUNTIME_PROFILE=1` to get per-kernel timings in logs; CI didn't have that enabled, I copied logs from a canary VM:
```
[profile] kernel=attention_kernel_tiled time_ms=1.72 calls=2345
[profile] kernel=attention_kernel_generic time_ms=0.42 calls=2345
[profile] kv_memmove time_ms=0.94 calls=2345
[overall] p95_decode_ms=118
```

sam: that's pretty clear. Tiled kernel is ~4x slower per-call for shortseq in that config and we add memmove.

tanvi: bisect update: narrowed to two commits within PR — 9f3cbd6 (selector baseline) and e8a4d2a (packing optimizer). 9f3cbd6 flips selector, e8a4d2a added prefetch memmove optimization that interacts w/ tiled kernel layout.

maria: if it's the interaction, simple revert of e8a4d2a from the canary might fix quickly while we craft better heuristics. Can we patch canary?

jake: I can hotfix canary image: build with e8a4d2a reverted, push, and run CI reproducer. ETA ~45m.

deploy-bot: Build pipeline started for image canary-hotfix-507777.

ci-bot: quick perf check queued: perf/serve/shortseq (batch16/seq24)

maria: thanks. If hotfix restores p95 to ~65ms we'll schedule a proper revert and follow-up issue for selector+prefetch interplay.

sam: add an eval and microbench in PR checklist to catch this class of regression: shortseq packing *and* memmove costs.

jake: update: hotfix image pushed, running repro now.

deploy-bot: Canary canary-hotfix-507777 deployed to canary pool.

ci-bot: quick perf check result: baseline=62ms hotfix=67ms current=67ms (pass). Regression resolved on hotfix image.

maria: great — revert + ship follow-up perf tuning. Opening revert PR and an issue for a safer selector (link: https://redwood/internal/issue/INFR-2971).

sam: also add telemetry for kernel_choice and memmove_estimate to runtime logs so we can monitor in prod without perf runs.

maria: filing a short postmortem in the release thread and scheduling a sync with the runtime team tomorrow. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
